title: Investigating Multi-Cultural Value Selection Biases in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.31199v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) serve users whose cultural identities are multi-layered, yet cultural evaluations commonly reduce identity to one label. In this work, we study LLMs under simultaneous identity cues, with a country persona in the system prompt and a second identity signaled in the user turn, either by naming a country (explicit cue) or through the query language (implicit cue). We test World Values Survey (WVS) multiple-choice probing and open-ended sociopolitical generation. In multiple-choice probing, language cues shift answers about three times more than explicit cues but away from the associated country's distribution, and explicit cues do not consistently move answers toward the named country. Across 1.6 million open-ended responses, naming a country closes 30-44% of the gap to the model's own responses for that country, and explicit cues produce more differentiated value changes than language cues. translated_title: 研究大语言模型中的多元文化价值观选择偏差
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）服务的用户具有多层次的文化身份，然而文化评估通常将身份简化为单一标签。在这项工作中，我们研究了LLM在同时存在多重身份线索时的表现，其中系统提示中包含一个国家角色设定，而用户轮次中通过两种方式传达第二种身份：直接命名一个国家（显式线索）或通过查询语言本身（隐式线索）。我们测试了世界价值观调查（WVS）多项选择探测和开放式社会政治内容生成两种方法。在多项选择探测中，语言线索对答案的偏移影响约为显式线索的三倍，但答案偏离了相关国家的价值观分布，而显式线索并不能持续地将答案推向所命名的国家的价值观。在160万条开放式回复中，命名一个国家可以缩小模型自身回复与该国价值观分布之间差距的30-44%，并且显式线索比语言线索产生更明显的价值观变化。我们的结果表明……
tldr: 该研究揭示了LLM在多重文化身份线索下存在价值观选择偏差：语言线索对答案的偏移是显式国家提示的三倍但反而偏离目标国家的价值观分布，而显式命名国家能缩小与该国价值观分布差距的30-44%并产生更明显的价值观变化。
en_tdlr: This study reveals value selection biases in LLMs under simultaneous multi-cultural identity cues: language cues shift answers three times more than explicit country naming but away from the named country's value distribution, while explicitly naming a country closes 30-44% of the gap to that country's values and produces more differentiated value shifts.
